title: Deliver an unfamiliar report

outcomes.can: Keep separate counts for separate things.
Deliver a complete solution to an unfamiliar request without help.

intro: This last module is an assessment. The request is new, and it uses ideas from the whole course: checking input, counting, handling a source that fails, and writing a check that catches a known bug. Reading a finished solution can explain an approach, but it does not show that you can solve the task yourself. Use the contract in the prompt to decide when your work is complete.

steps.title: Read the request before writing
steps.text: An import audit reads rows and reports how many were accepted, how many repeated an accepted Id, and how many were invalid. The three counts measure different things, and every row belongs to exactly one of them. Before writing code, take two or three small inputs and work out the report by hand. Those become your first checks. Decide the order of your tests too: whether a row is invalid has to be settled before asking whether it is a repeat.

steps.title: Predict the result
steps.text: The loop counts repeats separately from the Ids it has seen. Predict the two lines of output.

steps.title: Trace the result
steps.text: seen.Add returns false for the second "A", so duplicates becomes 1 and the set stays at two values. The repeat is counted once, and it does not add to the count of different Ids. The audit needs the same care, with a third count for rows that are invalid.

steps.title: Audit a task import
steps.text: Work from the contract in the prompt. There are no steps to follow. Save to check the complete submission. Any correct solution is accepted.

questions.prompt: What are the two lines of output?

choices.feedback: There are two different Ids, and one row repeated an Id that was already seen.
A set keeps each value once, so its Count is 2.
Only the second "A" is a repeat. The first one was new.

review.evidence: Open a fresh starter on a later visit, with the earlier answer closed. A first unaided pass on every case is later evidence of the skill. A hinted pass stays recorded as assisted.

drillGap: No practice drill covers a combined task. This assessment is the evidence for the module.
